question: Mesalazine (5-aminosalicylic acid) is the cornerstone of induction and maintenance therapy for mild-to-moderate ulcerative colitis but has limited proven efficacy in Crohn's disease.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is TRUE. The mucosal and predominantly colonic distribution of aminosalicylate activity matches the pathological pattern of UC (continuous mucosal inflammation, colon) but poorly matches Crohn's disease (transmural, patchy, any gut segment). This distinction directly drives drug selection in IBD.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Mesalazine acts topically on colonic mucosa by inhibiting NF-κB and reducing pro-inflammatory eicosanoid production. Its efficacy is well-established in UC (mucosal, colonic) but evidence for Crohn's disease (transmural, can affect any segment) is weak — guidelines do not recommend 5-ASA drugs as standard Crohn's therapy.
